text: Understanding Git branching is an important skill for developers. A branch lets you work on new features without affecting the main code. When you start a task, you create a feature branch and make your changes there. This keeps the main branch safe and stable. When your work is finished, you merge the feature branch back into the main branch. Many teams also use pull requests, which allow others to review your code before merging. This creates a clear version control workflow where everyone can see changes and work together. Learning these steps helps you collaborate better and avoid mistakes in your projects.
